name: Rapa Nui National Park
description: Rapa Nui National Park covers much of Easter Island, a remote Chilean island in the southeastern Pacific. Polynesian settlers arrived around A.D. 300, and between the 10th and 16th centuries their descendants carved and raised hundreds of giant stone figures called moai, many standing on shrine platforms. Today the park is managed by the island's Indigenous Rapa Nui community.
